title: Assemble training data
action: Collect the experimental electrostrictive coefficients d1111, d1122, d1212 for ten NaCl-type alkali halides (LiF, NaF, NaCl, NaBr, KCl, KBr, KI, RbCl, RbBr, RbI) from Bohatý and Haussühl (1977), average values for LiF and NaCl where multiple datasets exist, discarding outliers as per the paper. Also collect the material constants: static and high-frequency dielectric constants (ε(0), ε(∞)) from Lowndes and Martin (1969), the heteropolar band gap C from Levine (1973), and the lattice constant a from Landolt-Börnstein (1973).

title: Compute relative bond change (Q/d) for training crystals
action: Using the material constants from step 1 and physical constants (permittivity of free space, electron charge, reduced Planck constant, electron mass), compute the plasma frequency and the Szigeti effective charge, then compute Q/d for each training crystal via the formula relating ε(0), ε(∞), a, C, and an assumed electric field E = 1 V/m.

title: Fit empirical linear relations
action: Perform ordinary least-squares regression of experimental d1111, d1122, d1212 (from step 1) against (Q/d)^2 (from step 2) to obtain the slopes and intercepts for the linear relations d = slope * (Q/d)^2 + intercept.
description: Fitted coefficients for linear models of the three electrostrictive coefficients.
output_schema: Header: coefficient_type,slope,intercept. All values in scientific notation. Slopes are in 10^{-20} m^2 V^{-2} per dimensionless (Q/d)^2, intercepts in 10^{-20} m^2 V^{-2}.

title: Predict electrostrictive coefficients for target crystals
action: Assemble the material constants for LiCl, LiBr, NaI, KF, RbF from the same literature sources. Compute (Q/d) for these five crystals using the same methods as in step 2. Apply the linear relations from step 3 to the computed (Q/d)^2 to predict d1111, d1122, d1212 for each target crystal.
description: Predicted quadratic electrostrictive coefficients for five alkali halide crystals.
output_schema: Header: crystal,d1111,d1122,d1212. All values in scientific notation, units 10^{-20} m^2 V^{-2}.
